pr_title: Fix Samsung TV state when the device is turned off
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
Fixes a bug where newer models report a `on` state every 50 minutes (as described in #35629)
This PR checks the `PowerState` field from the device info returned by the TV to check the actual state of the device. Nothing changes for older TV models that don't support websockets.

Hey there @escoand, @chemelli74, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`samsungtv`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L798) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

> Fixes a bug where newer models report a `on` state every 50 minutes (as described in #35629) 

Are you sure all models report this info ?
And even more important: are you sure is a real improvement ? IF the check is every 50min, I think that the current test of connecting every 20 secs is much more precise.

Do I miss something ?

Simone

> > Fixes a bug where newer models report a `on` state every 50 minutes (as described in #35629)
> 
> Are you sure is a real improvement ? IF the check is every 50min, I think that the current test of connecting every 20 secs is much more precise.
> 
> Do I miss something ?
> 
> Simone

The check is implemented inside the is_on method, so it returns a precise result (I didn't add any separate check method for what I described)

> Are you sure all models report this info ?

I wasn't able to find much documentation about that. [This](https://developer.samsung.com/smarttv/develop/extension-libraries/smart-view-sdk/receiver-apps/debugging.html) is something similar to what the library uses. However, if the `PowerState` field isn't returned by the TV, it is considered a `on` device since it returned a reponse (same as before). I only tested it on my TV and it works perfectly, but if other TVs don't support it, they get treated according to the current logic.

@chemelli74 I'm not entirely sure why the test fails...
`fd4b88a` passed all the checks when I submitted it for the first time, but apparently there's something wrong with the `home-assistant-frontend==20220126.0` requirement
My TV, that use the `websocket` method, doesn't report `PowerState`.

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Samsung TV integration appears as if the TV is turning on and off every ~50 minutes.

This is with a Samsung Q80R TV.  I dont see any message about this model being supported but I was able to add it manually and it does show the correct status when it is on and off plus I can switch inputs or use "wake on lan" to turn it on and off functions normally as well!  The only quirks are the Name is not passed through and this on/off blip every 50 minutes.

See screenshot here:  https://i.imgur.com/Uz77KFq.png

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61300332/81966939-d3b01780-95df-11ea-97f5-1c2c5773f88c.png)

-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.109.6
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Hassio
- Integration causing this issue: Samsung TV
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/samsungtv/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`


review_comments: We need a test for this and one for when the key isn’t present as not all models are likely to have this given the wide array of firmwares

Not really sure what tests should I add. Should I add tests for the state with and without `PowerState`? I tried to take a look at the existing tests but I'm a bit confused.

I enabled edits in case someone wants to point me in the right direction 😄

You already have tests without `PowerState`, so you shouldn't change those (ensures compatibility).
Instead you should add a single new test with PowerState added to the device info.

Your current implementation assumes that if `PowerState` is absent, then the TV is offline (`return False)`.
Instead, it should fallback to the previous implemenation (`return self._get_remote() is not None`)

```suggestion
            return self._get_remote() is not None
```

Note: I have PR #67216 in progress, which also makes `is_on` abstract. As soon as that one is merged, then you will need to rebase this PR.
